policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'and she crieth out' preserves both καί and the present tense of κράζει, excluding omission of καί and imperfect ἔκραζεν.
ASV order 'a great red dragon' follows μέγας πυρρός; both alternatives reverse the adjectives.
Both ἄρσεν and ἄρρενα denote the male child and are compatible with ASV 'a man child'; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'prepared of God' does not reliably distinguish agency expressed with ἀπό from ὑπό; retain the base fallback.
ASV modal 'may nourish' supports subjunctive τρέφωσιν or ἐκτρέφωσιν and excludes indicative τρέφουσιν, but English 'nourish' does not distinguish the two subjunctives; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'going forth to war' may render the articular infinitive or supply the same expansion without τοῦ; retain the base fallback.
ASV plural 'they prevailed not' directly reflects ἴσχυσαν rather than singular ἴσχυσεν.
ASV plural possessive 'their place' directly reflects αὐτῶν rather than singular αὐτῷ.
ASV has no English article before the proper name 'Satan,' as expected whether Greek ὁ is present or absent; retain the base fallback.
Both κατήγωρ and κατήγορος mean 'accuser' and ASV does not distinguish the forms; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'who accuseth them' is compatible with accusative αὐτούς and genitive αὐτῶν under this verb; retain the base fallback.
ASV vocative 'O heavens' does not establish whether Greek οἱ is present; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'Woe for the earth and for the sea' reflects the accusative pair τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν rather than the dative alternative.
ASV 'the two wings' may supply an English article whether Greek αἱ is present or omitted; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'where she is nourished' directly reflects ὅπου τρέφεται rather than purpose clause ὅπως τρέφηται.
